text.name: TextDesc2
text.text: The Acorn Electron was an 8-bit home computer released in 1983 by Acorn Computers as a lower-cost version of the BBC Micro. It used the same 6502-based architecture and BBC BASIC programming language while offering a smaller design aimed at home users and education. The system featured advanced graphics modes for its price range and supported a large library of games and software through cassette storage and later disk expansions. Although less powerful than the BBC Micro, the Electron became a popular British home computer.
